describes: the Asterism wire protocol 1 as asterism 0.7.0 speaks it (docs/protocol.md)

values.note: every integer form of 1 is the same value
the largest integer of the protocol
the smallest integer of the protocol
float32 is read as a float (answered as float64)
a float with an integral value stays a float
str8 is the shortest form; str16 and str32 are read too
a str carries bytes; a receiver keeps them as they came, also when they are not UTF-8
binary data: bin, read as bytes and sent back as bin
str and int are the portable keys
outside the signed 64-bit range: not a value of the protocol
ext types are not values of the protocol
times are int nanoseconds since the epoch by convention, not the timestamp ext

incoming.id: call with an empty kwargs map

incoming.note: a keyword given as nil and a keyword left out are different on the wire (the callee's default applies to the absent one)
the message is the language's own
room for later additions to the request
the class name and message of the exception the method raised

map: no object nothing exposed by iut/conf

incoming.id: call returns what cannot be sent

incoming.note: the callee learns the caller from the key's last chunk
the caller chunk is a claim: only a router's access control makes it binding

incoming.id: malformed: kwargs with an int key

incoming.note: a payload is exactly one value
a call on protocol 0's key is refused at once, whatever its payload
the caller chunk must be a name: a wildcard is not answered (the method is not run)
the reply key is the object's own key, not the query's
arity -1: any number of arguments (exposed without counts)
one reply per exposed object, in any order
no reply (the caller sees nobody answer)
@profile is a verbatim chunk: ** does not reach it, and nothing else answers asterism/<node>/**
a wildcard node does reach it
the name is a str; the Ruby implementations also take a bin name by its bytes (answered 5)

outgoing.note: the caller's node ID is the call key's last chunk
keyword names and Symbol values go as str
Symbols, also as map keys, go as str; they come back as str
a binary String goes as a bin, and a bin comes back as one
RemoteError with the kind, class name and message as they came

outcome: the return value: cannot send a Object
